program.title: Basketball Point Guard Ankle Resilience & Movement Foundation

athlete_analysis.profile_summary: Beginner Point Guard with mild ankle injury history (rolling ankle). Single session per week, 60 min gym capacity. Needs low-impact, controlled single-leg work and ankle stability without high-volume plyometrics.
primary_constraints: History of ankle rolling—avoid rapid cutting, uncontrolled landing, high-impact volume
1 session/week limits volume; must prioritize transfer movements
Gym + court access; dumbbells and bands available
sport_demands: Point Guard: repeated acceleration, deceleration, lateral cuts, ball handling during movement, court transitions
Ankle stability critical for safe change-of-direction and landing control
Single-leg control and hip stability needed for pivot footwork and isolation moves
athlete_analysis.block_priority: Build ankle stiffness, hip control, and deceleration capacity in controlled single-leg patterns. Prepare for full-speed court transitions with pain-free landing mechanics and trunk stability during dribble penetration.

weeks.theme: Ankle Stiffness, Single-Leg Strength, Deceleration Setup

workouts.title: PG Ankle Resilience & Deceleration Base
sport_transfer: Loaded ankle plantarflexion builds calf resilience for cuts and push-offs without rolling risk
Single-leg stepping trains deceleration landing control for court transitions and defensive slides
Anti-rotation core bracing protects spine during dribble penetration and cross-body passes
workouts.why_this_session: Single weekly session must address Point Guard ankle fragility and deceleration control. Avoid plyometric volume; use strength-based single-leg work to prepare for safe court speed.

warmup.name: Bird Dog
warmup.purpose: Activate trunk stiffness and anti-rotation stability before loaded work

warmup.name: Dead Bug
warmup.purpose: Supine core activation and hip flexor control before standing movements

warmup.name: Lateral Band Walk
warmup.purpose: Hip abductor activation for single-leg stability and cutting readiness

main_work.name: Standing Calf Raise
main_work.purpose: Build loaded ankle plantarflexion strength and calf stiffness for push-off and ankle stability during cuts
main_work.load_guidance: Dumbbells: choose load for RPE 6-7 at rep 12; full range stretch at bottom, full lockout at top

main_work.name: Dumbbell Split Squat
main_work.purpose: Unilateral leg strength and single-leg control without stepping deceleration demands; teaches hip/knee/ankle alignment under load
main_work.load_guidance: Dumbbells at sides; RPE 6-7; long stable stance, weight distributed through whole front foot

main_work.name: Step-Up
main_work.purpose: Single-leg deceleration and loading in stepping pattern; transfers to court transitions and defensive positioning
main_work.load_guidance: Dumbbells in hand or at sides; box 12-16 inches; place whole foot on box; RPE 6-7

main_work.name: Tall-Kneeling Pallof Press
main_work.purpose: Anti-rotation core stability and trunk stiffness during offset loading; prepares trunk for dribble-penetration balance and contact tolerance
main_work.load_guidance: Band or light cable; RPE 5-6; knees hip-width, rib stacked over pelvis

cooldown.name: Deep Squat Pry
cooldown.purpose: Restore hip and ankle mobility post-strength work; maintain squat pattern range

cooldown.name: Side Plank from Knees
cooldown.purpose: Anti-lateral flexion hold; closes session with trunk stiffness reinforcement
cooldown.load_guidance: Knees bent and stacked; shoulders stacked over elbow

injury_modifications: If ankle plantarflexion pain occurs during standing calf raise, reduce range or substitute bodyweight Seated Calf Raise to maintain strength without end-range stress
If ankle inversion pain triggers during step-up or split squat, reduce box height, use band ankle support, or narrow stance width to limit plantarflexion demand
If pain-free range is limited, perform all work within pain-free range only; do not force ROM; focus on strength at available depth

weeks.progression_rule: Establish pain-free single-leg control and loaded hip/ankle stability. Use split stance and step patterns to teach deceleration without high-impact volume. Prepare ankle for court changes of direction.

program.nutrition_focus: Support recovery and ankle tissue health. Ensure adequate protein (1.6-2.0 g/kg) for strength adaptation; include anti-inflammatory foods (omega-3, berries, leafy greens); hydration for joint mobility.
recovery_focus: Sleep: Maintain 7h nightly to support neuromuscular adaptation and ankle healing
Post-session: Ankle ice or compression 10-15 min if swelling occurs; elevate if needed
Mobility snacks: 2-3 min lateral band walks or deep squats on off-days to maintain hip/ankle range
safety_notes: Ankle history of rolling: Avoid rapid uncontrolled direction changes, sprints without warm-up, and plyometric volume until pain-free single-leg control is demonstrated
Foot placement critical: All single-leg work requires whole foot on ground; partial weight on toes increases inversion risk
Pain-free rule: Stop any exercise if sharp ankle pain occurs; modify load, range, or stance before resuming
assumptions: No current pain; ankle history is remote and managed with controlled load progressions
Dumbbells and band access confirmed; no barbell or machine requirement this week
Point Guard role prioritizes ball-handling during movement; strength session complements court skill practice, not replaces it
1 session/week is entry-level commitment; coach may add court-based movement literacy work separately
